of registers.\n140\tTo avoid misuse of `always_ff` blocks, only the following macros shall be used to describe sequential behavior.\n141\tThe use of linter rules that flag explicit uses of `always_ff` in source code is encouraged.\n142\t\n143\t|    Macro     |                             Arguments                             |                                Description `arstn_sig`               | *deprecated* Flip-flop with asynchronous active-low reset                 |\n148\t| <code>`FFSR</code>   | `q_sig`, `d_sig`, `rst_val`, `clk_sig`, `rst_sig`                 | Flip-flop with synchronous active-high reset                              |\n149\t| <code>`FFSRN</code>  | `q_sig`, `d_sig`, `rst_val`, `clk_sig`, `rstn_sig`                | Flip-flop with synchronous active-low reset                               |\n150\t| <code>`FFNR</code>   | `q_sig`, `d_sig`, `clk_sig`                                       | Flip-flop without reset [`assertions.svh`](include/common_cells/assertions.svh) contains macros that expand to assertion blocks.\n166\tThese macros should recduce the effort in writing many assertions and make it\n167\teasier to use them. They are similar to but incompatible with the macros used by [lowrisc](https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/master/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_assert.sv).\n168\t\n169\t#### Simple Assertion and Cover Macros\n170\t| Macro              | Arguments                                        | Description                                                                |\n171\t| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n172\t| <code>`ASSERT_I</code>     | `__name`, `__prop`, (`__desc`)                   | Immediate assertion                                                        |\n173\t| <code>`ASSERT_INIT</code>  | `__name`, `__prop`, (`__desc`)                   | Assertion in initial block. Can be used for things like parameter checking |\n174\t| <code>`ASSERT_FINAL</code> | `__name`, `__prop`, (`__desc`)                   | Assertion in final block                                                   |\n175\t| <code>`ASSERT</code>       | `__name`, `__prop`, (`__clk`, `__rst`, `__desc`) | Assert a concurrent property directly                                      |\n176\t| <code>`ASSERT_NEVER</code> | `__name`, `__prop`, (`__clk`, `__rst`, `__desc`) | Assert a concurrent property NEVER happens                                 |\n177\t| <code>`ASSERT_KNOWN</code> | `__name`, `__sig`, (`__clk`, `__rst`, `__desc`)  | Concurrent clocked assertion with custom error message                     |\n178\t| <code>`COVER</code>        | `__name`, `__prop`, (`__clk`, `__rst`)           | Cover a concurrent property                                                |\n179\t- *The name of the clock and reset signals for implicit variants is `clk_i` and `rst_ni`, respectively.*\n180\t- *`__desc` is an optional string argument describing the failure causing the assertion to be violated that is embedded into the error report and defaults to `\"\"`.*\n181\t\n182\t#### Complex Assertion Macros\n183\t| Macro                 | Arguments                                                                           | Description                                                                                                |\n184\t| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n185\t| <code>`ASSERT_PULSE</code>    | `__name`, `__sig`, (`__clk`, `__rst`, `__desc`)                                     | Assert that signal is an active-high pulse with pulse length of 1 clock cycle                              |\n186\t| <code>`ASSERT_IF</code>       | `__name`, `__prop`, `__enable`, (`__clk`, `__rst`, `__desc`)                        | Assert that a property is true only when an enable signal is set                                           |\n187\t| <code>`ASSERT_KNOWN_IF</code> | `__name`, `__sig`, `__enable`, (`__clk`, `__rst`, `__desc`)                         | Assert that signal has a known value (each bit is either '0' or '1') after reset if enable is set          |\n188\t| <code>`ASSERT_STABLE</code>   | `__name`, `__valid`, `__ready`, `__data`, `__enable`, (`__clk`, `__rst`, `__desc`)  | Assert that the data on a ready-valid interface is kept stable after valid is asserted, until ready is too |\n189\t- *The name of the clock and reset signals for implicit variants is `clk_i` and `rst_ni`, respectively.*\n190\t- *`__desc` is an optional string argument describing the failure causing the assertion to be violated that is embedded into the error report and defaults to `\"\"`.*\n191\t\n192\t#### Assumption
